ddl:
CREATE TABLE user (
    account_creation_time DATETIME,
    account_update_time DATETIME,
    email VARCHAR(255),
    full_name VARCHAR(255),
    password VARCHAR(255),
    qq_number INTEGER,
    remarks INTEGER,
    user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    user_name VARCHAR(255),
    wechat_open_id INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE attraction (
    attraction_creation_time DATETIME,
    attraction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    attraction_name VARCHAR(255),
    details VARCHAR(255),
    era VARCHAR(255),
    images BLOB,
    reference_price INTEGER,
    region VARCHAR(255),
    type VARCHAR(255),
    update_time DATETIME
);

CREATE TABLE message (
    message_content VARCHAR(255),
    message_creation_time DATETIME,
    message_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    update_time DATETIME,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE ticket_booking (
    attraction_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    booking_date DATETIME,
    order_creation_time DATETIME,
    order_status VARCHAR(255),
    order_update_time DATETIME,
    remarks INTEGER,
    ticket_quantity INTEGER,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, attraction_id, order_update_time),
    FOREIGN KEY (attraction_id) REFERENCES attraction(attraction_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE attraction_comment (
    attraction_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    comment_content VARCHAR(255),
    comment_creation_time DATETIME,
    comment_update_time DATETIME,
    review_status VARCHAR(255),
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, attraction_id, comment_creation_time),
    FOREIGN KEY (attraction_id) REFERENCES attraction(attraction_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE attraction_favorite (
    attraction_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    favorite_creation_time DATETIME,
    favorite_update_time DATETIME,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, attraction_id, favorite_creation_time),
    FOREIGN KEY (attraction_id) REFERENCES attraction(attraction_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id)
);
gold_question: The system shall manage user basic information, including username, password, WeChat Open ID, name, QQ number, email, remarks, and the creation and update time of the account. The system shall also manage attraction information, including attraction name, details, reference price, images, era, type, region, and the creation and update time of the attraction. Users shall be able to book attraction tickets, with order information including user, attraction, booking date, ticket quantity, remarks, order status, and the creation and update time of the order. Users shall be able to comment on attractions, with comment information including user, attraction, comment content, review status, and the creation and update time of the comment. Users shall be able to leave messages on the platform, with message information including user, message content, and the creation and update time of the message. Additionally, users shall be able to favorite attractions of interest, with favorite information including user, attraction, and the creation and update time of the favorite.
nl_text: The rschema_0430 database contains six tables, each with its own unique purpose. The user table stores information about the users of the system, including their email, full name, password, and other personal details. The attraction table contains information about the attractions available for booking, including their name, details, era, region, type, and reference price. The message table stores messages sent between users, along with the time they were sent and the user who sent them. The ticket_booking table tracks the bookings made by users for specific attractions, including the attraction ID, booking date, order status, and ticket quantity. The attraction_comment table stores comments left by users about specific attractions, along with the user ID and comment content. Finally, the attraction_favorite table stores information about which attractions are favorited by users, including the attraction ID, favorite creation time, and user ID. Each table has its own set of columns, with some columns serving as primary keys, foreign keys, or unique constraints. The database is designed to ensure data integrity and referential integrity, with each table referencing other tables through foreign keys and constraints.
